findings.diagnosis: The prompt treats cuts immediately after scope-bearing operators (negation, modals, auxiliaries) as uniformly risky and therefore demotes them indiscriminately.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_767','en_us_1118','en_us_936'] — each shows a policy cut following or splitting around an auxiliary/conditional that produced a high contra or contra_kill; the offline targets only avoid those cuts when the left fragment would alone assert something the remainder could plausibly reverse.

edit.text: - Only demote cuts after scope-bearing operators when the left fragment, read alone, would assert a proposition the remainder could plausibly negate or reverse.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt over-corrects by pushing cuts rightward into short complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases in dense (low-latency) settings, which harms cohesion.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_651','en_us_1527','en_us_1137'] — all show the policy moving cuts into multiword names or short complements (to keep operators attached) and suffering lower cohesion/H_set in short–medium latency bins compared with targets that preserve compact phrases.

edit.text: - In dense/short-latency contexts, avoid shifting cuts into short complements or inside noun/prepositional phrases; prefer keeping multiword names and short noun phrases intact to preserve referent cohesion.
